title: Python recall gap: raise incoming-call recall of the native Python indexer, designed from Python semantics (DEC-303 (a19))
description: The S8 gate run (GCLI-83, 2026-11-25) FAILED on both repositories: click 68/80 = 0.8500 (Wilson lower 0.7559), requests 57/65 = 0.8769 (Wilson lower 0.7755), against recall >= 0.9 with Wilson lower >= 0.8 (DEC-303 (a2), (a5)); precision passed. DEC-303 (a19) (ODOC-640): the thresholds stand; the click and requests samples are spent as held-out evidence and are REFUSED as development data; this task is designed from Python's semantics under (a11), never from the per-site misses in those samples, and glyph-cli does not open the per-site misses of the click or requests ground truth to design it. Any later claim that glyph passes needs a FRESH blind sample drawn and classified before any analyzer run under the (a2) and (a3) conventions. The 0.1.0 tag and publish stay HELD pending the operator's release-scope question (dec-13m90z3).

HANDOFF 9 ADDENDUM: DEC-303 (a25) (2026-11-25 14:46Z, opum-ai/opum-doc#1966, ODOC-640), on the Opus delta's precision finding for GCLI-89. GCLI-89 is approved as built; this is a follow-up RULE, not a defect in #139. With the attribute-target defect fixed the analyzer can resolve a wrong edge where an attribute write shadows the target (self.m = f; self.m(); self.__class__ = Other; self.m(); k.m = f; k.m(); in-module monkeypatches mod.f = g, Cls.meth = g). Rule, by (a22) item 2 (every binding enumerable from the text; an attribute write is a binding of that attribute): (1) a write to self.m or cls.m in any method of a class, or to Cls.m anywhere in the module, makes calls through self, cls or Cls to attribute m of that class unresolved, counted as multiply bound; subclasses inherit the same treatment. (2) A write to mod.f inside the module that defines f, or in a module that imports it, makes calls to f resolved through that module unresolved, counted the same way. (3) A write to self.__class__ anywhere in a class leaves every self and type(self) receiver in that class unresolved. (4) A write to x.m on a local x bound under R4 or E1 makes x.m() unresolved. (5) Writes from outside the analysed modules, and setattr with a non-literal name, stay the accepted blind spot; setattr(obj, "m", v) with a literal name counts as a write to obj.m. BUILD ORDER: goes in with the admitted groups, after (a23) item 6's fixture, with red-before and green-after fixtures for each case; it must be in place before the fresh blind sample (it bears on precision). The unsampled category (bare-name calls reported as rebound after obj.helper = v) is GCLI-90, no ruling needed.
